title: Latency/Cost Signature–Driven Split Tests for Pin-Protected Model Revisions
creator: Priya Menon
description:
Problem: When we swap pinned model revisions, naive traffic canaries and A/B tests fail to surface regressions that only appear under specific request signatures (e.g., long-context, streaming-heavy, high temperature) or have uneven cost/latency distributions. Current pin-driven rollouts risk either (a) over-exposing expensive/slow variants or (b) masking performance regressions by sampling a non-representative traffic slice.

Proposal: Implement a Latency/Cost Signature–Driven Split Test (LCSS) framework that: (1) computes a compact request signature at the router (token_length bucket, streaming vs non-streaming, expected kv-cache hit heuristic, estimated token-cost class), (2) exposes a pin-level policy that stratifies canary traffic by signature buckets, and (3) runs paired A/B evaluations across those buckets to provide balanced, budget-aware validation of pinned revisions. The framework leverages published performance profiles for each model revision from the model catalog to select safe per-bucket exposures and to estimate expected cost deltas for rollout decisions.

Why novel: Unlike single-dimension canaries (percentage-only) or cohort holdouts, LCSS ensures the canary sees representative complexity and protects unit economics by limiting exposure in high-cost signatures while allowing broader validation in low-cost signatures. It also ties directly to the performance-profile publishing flow so PM/Eng can make decisions using model-backed expectations.
acceptance_criteria: Pin config supports a new 'signature_split_policy' field with per-bucket exposure percentages
Router computes request signature buckets for at least: short(<=64), medium(65-512), long(>512), streaming, high-temp (user-hot), kv-cache-miss-like heuristics
Canary A/B comparison UI shows per-bucket metrics (p50/p95 latency, token-cost delta, success rate, hallucination-rate) in Console
Automated rollout gates enforce rollback when any bucket exceeds thresholds (p95 latency +30% over baseline OR cost-per-token +25% OR error-rate +2%)
End-to-end test harness (eval set) runs paired samples for each bucket and produces a release recommendation report
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Design doc & perf-profile mapping (week 1) – DONE: design doc at https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/LCSS+Design
Phase 1: Router + policy plumbing (week 2-3) – implement signature computation in edge router and support 'signature_split_policy' in pin config (ENG)
Phase 2: Runtime safeguards (week 3-4) – budget caps per account, per-bucket exposure ceilings derived from model perf profiles
Phase 3: Console + telemetry (week 4-5) – per-pin per-bucket dashboard, simulated rollout preview
Phase 4: Eval harness + pilot (week 6) – run on 3 internal tenants with controlled workloads, compare to paired holdout baseline
Phase 5: Gradual ramp and GA (week 7-10) – promote to default pin rollout options after 1 month of stable telemetry
ui_changes: Pin configuration form: add 'Signature split policy' section with per-bucket sliders and a preview of estimated cost delta (based on selected model perf profile)
Console rollouts: add 'Bucket view' to canary page showing side-by-side metrics and traffic fractions
Simulate rollout: button to run a simulated split using recent traffic sample and show expected metric impact
Alerts page: new alert templates for bucket-based gates (latency/cost/error thresholds)
engineering_notes: Router must emit computed signature as structured tag in request trace for downstream aggregation (trace tag: lcss.signature)
Need small, lock-free in-memory map of perf-profiles (rev -> bucket expectations) to compute safe exposure ceilings
KV-cache compatibility: ensure pinned variant's cache warming plan is included in the pilot (ENG-41200 to own cache warming tests)
API: add pin-level API extension 'signature_split_policy' with schema documented in docs PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2345
Backfill: script to map historical request logs into signature buckets for initial dashboard baselining (data infra task)
risks: Signature misclassification may bias canary exposure—need conservative bucket definitions initially
Perf-profile mismatch: model catalog profiles are estimates; true tail behavior might differ under production multiplexing
Complexity in Console UX could overwhelm small customers—fallback to simple percentage-only policy should remain available
Billing edge cases: per-bucket caps must integrate with customer committed capacity to avoid surprise charges
